summary: For ages 7–9, teach the three periods of the Mesozoic Era in order (Triassic → Jurassic → Cretaceous) and the key idea that different dinosaurs lived in different periods, separated by vast spans of time, rather than all coexisting. The central anchor is that more time separates Stegosaurus (Late Jurassic, ~150 Mya) from T. rex (Late Cretaceous, ~66–69 Mya) — about 80 million years — than separates T. rex from us today (~66 million years), so the two never met.
misconceptions: 'All dinosaurs lived at the same time' — they are spread across ~150+ million years and mostly never overlapped.
'Stegosaurus and T. rex lived together / could have fought' — ~80 million years separated them; they never met.
'Dinosaurs and the very first mammals/humans are close in time' — T. rex is far closer to us than to Stegosaurus.
'The periods are short' — each period spans tens of millions of years.
'Older period = smaller/more primitive dinosaurs only' — giants and specialists existed across all three periods.

activities.title: Build the timeline and sort the dinosaurs
steps: Set up three slots left to right in order: Triassic, then Jurassic, then Cretaceous.

Sort a set of famous dinosaurs into the correct period: e.g. early dinosaurs/Plateosaurus into the Triassic; Stegosaurus, Brachiosaurus and Allosaurus into the Jurassic; T. rex, Triceratops and Velociraptor into the Cretaceous.

After placing Stegosaurus (Jurassic) and T. rex (Cretaceous), mark the distance between them on the timeline, then compare it to the distance from T. rex to a 'you, today' marker placed at the end of the line.
State in your own words whether Stegosaurus and T. rex could ever have met, and why.
activities.insight: The Age of Dinosaurs was not one crowded scene; different casts of dinosaurs lived and vanished across tens of millions of years, and the gap between two famous dinosaurs can exceed the gap between the later one and us.

activities.title: 'Who would win?' — the never-met challenge
steps: Pose the classic playground question: who would win in a fight — Stegosaurus or T. rex?
Before answering, locate each on the timeline and read off how far apart they lived.
Decide whether a fight was even possible, and explain the reasoning using the time gap.
Compare: was T. rex closer in time to Stegosaurus, or to you? Justify with the two gaps (~80 My vs ~66 My), kept as a comparison rather than a calculation.
activities.insight: Two famous dinosaurs people imagine fighting were separated by more time than separates the later one from the present, so staging their fight is impossible.

activities.title: Explain and probe deep time
steps: Answer true/false: there is more time between Stegosaurus and T. rex than between T. rex and you — and explain how you know.
Answer: which lived longer ago, Stegosaurus or T. rex, and how can you tell from the timeline?
Answer: could a Triassic dinosaur ever have met a Cretaceous one? Explain why or why not.
Respond to the prompt: 'Stegosaurus and T. rex must have fought because they were both dinosaurs living at the same time.' Say whether this is right and explain.
Explain in a sentence or two why the 'Age of Dinosaurs' (over ~150 million years) was an enormous span, not a single scene.
activities.insight: Chronological order of the periods plus the magnitude of the gaps together explain why dinosaurs separated by tens of millions of years, such as Stegosaurus and T. rex or a Triassic and a Cretaceous dinosaur, never coexisted.

checkQuestion: Someone says: 'Stegosaurus and Tyrannosaurus rex must have fought each other, because they were both dinosaurs living at the same time.' Are they right? Explain your answer.
checkAnswer: No. Stegosaurus lived in the Jurassic period and T. rex in the Cretaceous period — separated by around 80 million years. They never met. Different dinosaurs lived in different periods of the Mesozoic, and those periods span enormous stretches of time.
